title: Pick a clear training lock: hold light turning pressure with one hand while the other sets each pin
instruction: Pick the clear training lock open with the tension wrench and the hook pick, turn the plug to the green open mark, then take the pick out and move both grippers away.
context: Locksmiths open locks for lockout service by single-pin picking: steady light torque on the plug makes one pin bind at a time, and each binding pin is lifted until it sets. Releasing the torque drops the set pins, and forcing the plug does not open it.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y left, from the midpoint between them; heights above the table top. A clear pin-tumbler training lock, about 3x a real cylinder with 3 pin stacks, is clamped to the table on a dark 9.5 x 6.4 x 6.8 cm pedestal; its cut-away housing (9.5 cm long; only thin chamber fins are drawn) holds a clear round plug (40 mm diameter, 90 mm long, 110 g) whose axis runs along x, 10 cm above the table; the keyway face is at x 25 cm, y 0, facing the robot. The keyway is a 9 x 24 mm slot, 75 mm deep. Pin stacks at 35, 50 and 65 mm behind the face: 8 x 8 mm brass key pins (16 mm long) in the plug and red, green and blue driver pins (18 mm long) in the housing, each pushed down by a spring (0.3 N at rest, 30 N/m). A spring-steel tension wrench is fitted to the plug face: a dark lever pointing up and outward to the right (-y) at 45 degrees with an orange free-spinning sleeve (18 mm diameter, 30 mm long) on its end, 10 cm from the axis, centred at (22.3, -7.1) cm, 17.1 cm high. An orange pointer on the plug face shows the wrench's unflexed direction; a white tick on the housing marks the start and a green tick the open mark (90 degrees). A steel hook pick (4 x 4 mm shaft, 130 mm long, with a 7 mm upturned tooth at its tip, a 75 mm dog-leg to the left and a dark 10 x 30 x 40 mm upright handle plate, 50 g) lies on the table with its tip at (28, 12) cm pointing +x and its handle plate standing at (15.2, 19.5) cm. The plug starts at 0 degrees, all pins down; grippers open at the ready pose. The pin stacks are seen through the cut-away housing from the right arm's wrist camera while that gripper holds the wrench sleeve; at the top camera's resolution they are too small to read.
scoring: Measured at 20 Hz (photo/ruler equivalents in brackets). A pin is set when its driver's bottom is within 0.8 mm of the shear line (the plug's surface) and its key pin's top is at least 1 mm below it [the stack is visibly split at the shear line, the coloured driver resting on the plug]. 0.25 for each pin set at the same time for at least 0.5 s (the best count is kept). 1.0 (success, the trial ends) when the plug is turned at least 85 degrees [the orange pointer at the green open mark], the wrench is unloaded, flexed 3 degrees or less from the plug's pointer [wrench lined up with the orange pointer], the pick's tip is out of the keyway (1 cm in front of the face or 3 cm from the plug axis), and both grippers are at least 80% open and with each gripper centre at least 7 cm from the wrench sleeve centre and the keyway mouth [ruler], all for 2 s. The plug must first cross beyond its 15-degree binding region with all three pins set; after that, the drivers may drop into the open detents. Returning to the binding region requires a fresh valid crossing. Score 0, permanently, if that crossing bypasses an unset pin, if it turns below -15 degrees, if the wrench is ever flexed more than 15 degrees from the pointer (more than 0.15 N m: forcing the plug), the lock body moves more than 2 mm, or the state is non-finite.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Turn the plug back to 0 (the pins drop), straighten the wrench and lay the pick back on the table at its start pose.
fidelity: Enlarged (~3x), cut-away pin-tumbler trainer; square pins and exaggerated bore offsets make binding visible. Native rigid contacts and prismatic/revolute joints; declared pin, return and wrench springs. Wrench fitted to plug: no slip, wear or security pins. Open detents retain 90 degrees. The scripted demo uses simulator poses, pin heights and known binding order; evaluated policies receive camera images and joint state. Physics 240 Hz; scoring 20 Hz.
